name: GanttChart
description: Project timeline with dependency arrows, milestones, hierarchy tree pane, summary rollups, and a reject/accept/adjust drag commit gate.

api.name: GanttChart
api.description: Project timeline with dependency arrows, milestones, hierarchy tree pane, summary rollups, and a reject/accept/adjust drag commit gate.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description: Hoists this chart's GanttState store (design spec Phase 3, T4 — the REUI useGanttState analog). null (the default) keeps the PRIOR, fully self-contained behavior: an internally-owned instance, constructed once at mount, invisible to anything outside this component — byte-identical to every pre-T4 render (see _state's own remarks for the mount-time resolution and GanttChartRenderTests's own byte-identical golden-markup regression). Supplying an instance lets a consumer read/react to this chart's state externally and drive it imperatively (ScrollToTaskAsync/ScrollToDateAsync/SetViewMode), and lets multiple components share ONE instance (see GanttState's own attach/detach remarks for exactly what "sharing" means: every attached-or-not subscriber re-renders on any change; only ONE at a time is the imperative-API target). Read ONCE, at OnInitialized — like ViewMode's own mount seed, this is an "owned outright for the component's lifetime" parameter, not a reactively-rebound one (design spec "keep it simple" precedent, same rationale _state's predecessor field already used). Changing WHICH instance is bound after mount is deliberately out of T4's scope — a live swap would need to rebuild every per-instance reconcile-tracking field (_lastSnapshot/_tasksVersion/_viewModeIntent/etc.) against the new instance's already-committed values, which is a different, harder problem T4 does not need to solve to satisfy the plan's own contract ("nav and view rendered separately against ONE shared state instance must work" — a stable instance for the component's lifetime, not a reactive one).

parameters.name: Tasks
parameters.description: The tasks (and milestones) rendered as bars.

parameters.name: TasksChanged
parameters.description: Raised whenever the task set changes — either because Tasks genuinely changed, or because the user dragged/resized a bar in the chart (design spec Phase 2, T1 — v2-parity TasksChanged, same contract as v2's Gantt.TasksChanged).

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: The active zoom level. Two-way bindable via ViewModeChanged. Default Day.

parameters.name: ViewModeChanged
parameters.description: Raised when the user picks a new zoom level from GanttNav's toolbar.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: CSS max-height of the timeline's scrollable viewport. Default "500px".

parameters.name: TodayHighlight
parameters.description: Highlight today with an accent header label, header dot, and full-column tint (design spec Phase 3, T2 — master switch, see GanttTimeline.TodayHighlight's own remarks). Default true.

parameters.name: FirstDayOfWeek
parameters.description: Explicit first-day-of-week override for the Day-mode ISO week-band upper header (design spec Phase 3, T2). Null derives it from CurrentCulture.

parameters.name: OffDays
parameters.description: The week days treated as "off" for MarkOffDays (design spec Phase 3, T2). Null derives a region-appropriate set from CurrentCulture — see DefaultOffDays.

parameters.name: MarkOffDays
parameters.description: Tints OffDays columns (design spec Phase 3, T2). Default false — no v2 equivalent.

parameters.name: NowIndicator
parameters.description: Renders a precise current-time line in sub-day view modes (design spec Phase 3, T2). Default false.

parameters.name: BarHeight
parameters.description: Override the pixel height of each task bar (default DefaultBarHeight).

parameters.name: ColumnWidth
parameters.description: Override the pixel width of each date column for the current view mode.

parameters.name: BarColor
parameters.description: Per-task bar colour override — same contract as v2's Gantt.BarColor.

parameters.name: GroupBy
parameters.description: Optional grouping function. When set, tasks are sorted by group label (stable within a group) before rendering — mirrors v2's GroupBy sort. Visual group-header rows are a tree-pane (T3) concern, not built here.

parameters.name: BarTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces a bar's default label content when set.

parameters.name: OnTaskClick
parameters.description: Raised when a bar is activated via click or keyboard (Enter/Space) — same contract as v2's Gantt.OnTaskClick (Codex round 4, P2 #5).

parameters.name: ShowTreePane
parameters.description: Shows the left tree/list pane (design spec Phase 2, T3). Null (the default) resolves to DefaultShowTreePane: on when GroupBy is set or any task sets ParentId, off otherwise — a flat task list with neither gets the same single-pane layout T2 always rendered.

parameters.name: Readonly
parameters.description: Disables drag-to-move/-resize editing in the chart (design spec Phase 2, T1 — v2-parity Readonly). Default false.

parameters.name: OnDateChange
parameters.description: Raised after a task bar's start/end dates change via drag/resize, with the updated task (design spec Phase 2, T1 — v2-parity OnDateChange, same contract as v2's Gantt.OnDateChange). Also folded into TasksChanged.

parameters.name: OnTaskUpdate
parameters.description: Unified commit GATE (Phase 4 — the REUI onEventUpdate analog, upgraded from a Phase 1-3 post-commit notification to a real pre-commit gate as part of this promotion; see GanttUpdateResult's own remarks for why this is the ONE breaking change the promotion ships). Called for EVERY drag/resize/progress/create edit — GanttTaskUpdateSource discriminates which gesture — BEFORE anything commits to this chart's state, so a consumer can: Reject (Reject/false): nothing commits — no state change, no OnDateChange/OnProgressChange/OnTaskCreate, no TasksChanged. Accept (Accept/true): commits exactly the proposed Task — byte-identical to every Phase 1-3 "no handler wired up" render. Accept with an adjustment (AcceptWith): commits the proposal with Start/End/Progress substituted in — e.g. snapping a drag to a host's own business-hour grid. Leaving this null (the default) accepts every edit unconditionally, exactly like the pre-promotion "no handler" case. Synchronous by design — mirrors CanDrop's own established sync-Func shape (this component's live-drag validator) so the two "should this happen" hooks share one calling convention.

parameters.name: OnProgressChange
parameters.description: Raised after a task bar's progress changes via the progress handle (design spec Phase 2, T2 — v2-parity OnProgressChange, same contract as v2's Gantt.OnProgressChange). Also folded into TasksChanged.

parameters.name: CanDrop
parameters.description: Live scheduling drag-drop validator (design spec Phase 2, T2 — the REUI canDropEvent analog). See CanDrop for the full contract; passed straight through unchanged.

parameters.name: AllowCreate
parameters.description: Opt-in drag-create on empty track background (design spec Phase 2, T3 — a REUI-parity addition; v2 has no drag-create at all, so this defaults to false, keeping strict v2 parity until a caller opts in). Passed straight through to AllowCreate — see there for the full contract, including why Readonly always wins over it.

parameters.name: OnTaskCreate
parameters.description: Raised when a drag-create commits (design spec Phase 2, T3 — REUI parity; v2 has no equivalent). Fired alongside OnTaskUpdate (Source=Create) — mirrors how OnProgressChange/OnDateChange are each raised alongside OnTaskUpdate for their own gesture, per source, in HandleTaskUpdateAsync. Also folded into TasksChanged (the new task is APPENDED, not merged-by-id, for this source).

parameters.name: ShowSummaryBars
parameters.description: Renders a duration-weighted REUI-style envelope strip on every hierarchy-parent or flat-group row (design spec Phase 3, T3 — "Summary rollup bars, duration-weighted"). Default false — see ShowSummaryBars's own remarks for the reasoning (a deliberate v3-look delta from REUI's own default-on summaryBars, pinned in the Phase-3 ledger).

parameters.name: RollupMath
parameters.description: Overrides the default duration-weighted rollup math (design spec Phase 3, T3 — "Overridable rollup math"). See RollupMath for the full contract, including the defensive handling of a throwing or out-of-range override. Passed straight through, unchanged.

parameters.name: SummaryTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces a summary strip's default rendering when set (design spec Phase 3, T3 — the REUI renderSummary analog). Passed straight through to SummaryTemplate, unchanged.

parameters.name: ColorByGroup
parameters.description: Assigns each task a stable per-group palette colour when BarColor is null (design spec Phase 3, T7). Passed straight through to ColorByGroup — see its own remarks for the full default-off reasoning and the group-colour stability contract.

parameters.name: ShowOffscreenIndicators
parameters.description: Off-screen indicator chips at a row's edge, click-to-scroll (design spec Phase 3, T7). Passed straight through to ShowOffscreenIndicators — see its own remarks for the default-TRUE reasoning (the one deliberate exception to this campaign's default-off precedent for new REUI-parity look additions).

parameters.name: ShowZoomControl
parameters.description: Floating +/- zoom control in the canvas corner (design spec Phase 3, T7). Passed straight through to ShowZoomControl.

parameters.name: ZoomLevels
parameters.description: Restricts/orders which zoom levels BOTH GanttNav's toolbar switcher and ShowZoomControl's floating stepper offer (design spec Phase 3, T7 — fixes a pre-existing gap: GanttNav.ZoomLevels already existed but was never reachable through GanttChart's own surface before this task added a caller for it). Null (the default) shows the full default Day/Week/Month/Year set on both surfaces — see GanttZoomLevelModel for the exact resolution contract, including the Quarter-must-be-explicit rule.

parameters.name: WheelZoom
parameters.description: Ctrl/Cmd + wheel over the timeline zooms, anchored on the pointer position (ReUI parity — wheelZoom, defaulting true). A bare wheel is never touched — the page/pane keeps scrolling exactly as it would with no Gantt on it. Steps through ZoomLevels (the SAME resolved list ShowZoomControl's stepper and GanttNav's toolbar already step through — never a second, independently-tunable list); at the resolved list's own zoom limits the gesture is left alone entirely, so the browser's own ctrl/cmd+wheel page-zoom takes over instead of the gesture being silently swallowed. See WheelZoom's own remarks for the full "stepped, not continuous" design rationale.

parameters.name: TreeColumns
parameters.description: Extra tree-pane columns rendered after the pinned name column (design spec Phase 3, T5 — REUI "Multi-column task tree"). Null/empty (the default) renders exactly the single name column T2/T3 already did — byte-identical unless a caller opts in. See GanttTreeColumn for the per-column contract.

parameters.name: TreeHeaderMenu
parameters.description: Slot rendered in the tree pane's header row, after the column titles (design spec Phase 3, T5 — REUI "Columns menu in header slot"). Null (the default) renders nothing extra there.

parameters.name: RowTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces a row's default label-cell content when set (design spec Phase 3, T5). The indent spacer and expander/toggle button are ALWAYS rendered by GanttTree regardless — see its own remarks for why that chrome must survive a custom template or the tree becomes unusable. Only applies to TASK rows (GanttVisibleRow.Task non-null); a flat-grouping GanttRowKind.GroupHeader row has no task to feed it and always falls back to its own label.

parameters.name: ShowTaskMeta
parameters.description: Renders a second "date-range · N%" line under a tree row's name (2026-08-10 shadcn alignment plan, G6). Default false — see ShowTaskMeta's own remarks (this parameter is a straight pass-through). Ignored when RowTemplate is set.

parameters.name: TreePaneWidth
parameters.description: Controlled width (pixels) of the tree pane's pinned name column (design spec Phase 3, T5 — the resizable tree/timeline splitter). Null (the default) is UNCONTROLLED: the chart tracks its own width internally, starting at DefaultTreePaneWidth and persisting whatever the user last dragged it to for the rest of the component's lifetime (session-persistent, not just per-render). Every value — controlled or internally tracked — is clamped to [MinTreePaneWidth, MaxTreePaneWidth]. Controlled-ness is decided by THIS parameter's own nullability — NOT by whether TreePaneWidthChanged has a delegate (a bug found during T5's own disable-check pass: a caller may wire the callback purely to OBSERVE resizes while leaving this null, which must still behave as fully uncontrolled/session-persistent, not silently freeze). See TreePaneWidthChanged's own remarks for the controlled-veto contract (same "the drag must not fight the parameter" discipline as every other controlled/uncontrolled pair in this component).

parameters.name: TreePaneWidthChanged
parameters.description: Raised exactly once per completed splitter gesture (a pointer-drag release, or a keyboard nudge — never continuously while dragging; see GanttTree's own remarks for why the LIVE drag visual is JS-only and never round-trips through Blazor mid-gesture) with the new width, already clamped. Fires whenever a delegate is present, whether or not TreePaneWidth itself is set — notification and control are separate concerns (mirrors OnProgressChange/OnDateChange firing independent of TasksChanged). Control specifically is decided by TreePaneWidth's own nullability: when it is non-null (CONTROLLED) and the consumer does not update its own bound value in response to this callback, that is a veto — the NEXT render reverts the pane to whatever TreePaneWidth still holds, the same veto contract TasksChanged/ViewModeChanged already have. The drag never "fights" the parameter, because nothing round-trips through Blazor until the gesture is already over.

parameters.name: ShowRowCheckboxes
parameters.description: Renders a checkbox column in the tree pane (design spec Phase 3, T6 — REUI "Leaf row selection (checkboxes)"). Default false. Passed straight through to ShowRowCheckboxes.

parameters.name: SelectedIds
parameters.description: Controlled set of selected LEAF task ids (design spec Phase 3, T6 — two-way SelectedIds). null (the default) is UNCONTROLLED: the chart tracks its own selection internally via SelectedIds, starting empty. Same controlled-ness discipline as TreePaneWidth (decided by THIS parameter's own nullability, not by whether SelectedIdsChanged has a delegate — a caller may wire the callback purely to OBSERVE selection while leaving this null). Only LEAF task ids are ever members — see GanttSelectionModel's own remarks for exactly which rows qualify and why a hierarchy-parent's own id never appears here even when every one of its descendants is selected.

parameters.name: SelectedIdsChanged
parameters.description: Raised whenever the selection changes (a checkbox click — leaf toggle or parent/group select/deselect-descendants), with the FULL resulting set. Fires whenever a delegate is present, whether or not SelectedIds itself is set — notification and control are separate concerns (mirrors TreePaneWidthChanged's own remarks). Control specifically is decided by SelectedIds's own nullability: when non-null (CONTROLLED) and the consumer does not update its own bound value in response, that is a veto — the NEXT render reverts to whatever SelectedIds still holds.

parameters.name: AllowRowReorder
parameters.description: Enables drag-to-reorder tree rows (design spec Phase 3, T6 — REUI "Row reorder (drag tree rows)"). Default false. Passed straight through to AllowRowReorder — see its own remarks for the within-bucket-only scope (cross-parent/cross-group moves are ParentId edits, out of scope, never offered by the drag UI). Readonly blocks it unconditionally.

parameters.name: CanDropRow
parameters.description: Live validation predicate for a candidate row-reorder drop position (design spec Phase 3, T6 — the REUI canDropEvent analog applied to row reorder; see GanttScheduleDropContext's own remarks for why SCHEDULING drag validation — CanDrop — is a separate, differently-shaped parameter/type from this one). Passed straight through to CanDropRow, unchanged. Null (default) permits every within-bucket position.

parameters.name: OnRowReorder
parameters.description: Raised once, after a completed row-reorder drop, with the resolved GanttRowReorder payload (design spec Phase 3, T6). This component ALSO applies the equivalent list reorder to its own task set and pushes it through the SAME TasksChanged/controlled- veto pipeline every other edit (move/resize/progress/create) already uses — see HandleRowReorderAsync's own remarks for why the component mutates rather than merely reporting.

parameters.name: TrailingContent
parameters.description: Extra content rendered in GanttNav's toolbar, after the zoom switcher (design spec Phase 3, T8 — the GanttSettingsMenu companion's documented slot; v2 parity with Gantt.TrailingContent). Passed straight through to TrailingContent, unchanged.

parameters.name: DragGhostTemplate
parameters.description: Overrides the drag ghost's rendered content for every bar (design spec Phase 3, T8). Passed straight through to DragGhostTemplate — see its own remarks (and DragGhostTemplate's) for the full coordinate-space contract.

parameters.name: BarContextMenu
parameters.description: Renders a Lumeo ContextMenu at the pointer when a bar is right-clicked (design spec Phase 3, T8). Passed straight through to BarContextMenu — see its own remarks for the full contract, including why this is deliberately independent of Readonly.

parameters.name: InfiniteScroll
parameters.description: Nearing either horizontal edge of the currently-rendered range extends it by another page, preserving scroll position, instead of dead-ending (design spec Phase 3, T9 — "horizontal infinite scroll ... replaces v2's fixed pad-before/after"). Passed straight through to InfiniteScroll — see its own remarks. Default true (per the design spec's own literal wording) — DELIBERATE, decided the same way ShowOffscreenIndicators's own default-true was: what does an EXISTING (pre-T9) v3 consumer actually notice? Nothing, for any chart that never scrolls far enough to reach the range ComputeInitialRange/ApplyPadding already computed — those two methods are COMPLETELY unchanged by this parameter, so the chart's INITIAL render, and every render before a user scrolls near either padded edge, is byte-identical regardless of this default. The only observable delta is what happens ONCE that edge is reached: pre-T9 (and false), the timeline simply stops — native scrollWidth caps there, exactly v2's own fixed-padding behavior; default-true, it keeps going. That is a strictly ADDITIVE capability (you can now scroll further than before), never a visual "look changed on upgrade with no code change" surprise the way e.g. NowIndicator/MarkOffDays' own opt-in defaults exist to avoid (both of those touch EVERY row/column of an already-fully-visible chart unconditionally the moment they're on; infinite scroll only ever engages in direct response to the viewer's own continued scrolling, past a boundary nothing before T9 let them reach anyway). false restores v2 parity exactly (byte-matching fixed padding — see the Phase-3 ledger entry for the parity spec that proves it against both routes).

enums.name: GanttViewMode
enums.description: Gantt timeline zoom level. Supported by the Lumeo SVG engine: QuarterDay = 6-hour columns, HalfDay = 12-hour columns, Day = 1 column/day, Week = 1 column/week, Month = 1 column/month, Year = 1 column/year.

examples.title: A realistic project plan — hierarchy, dependencies & milestones
examples.code:
<GanttChart Tasks="_tasks" ViewMode="GanttViewMode.Day" Height="420px" />

@code {
    // ParentId builds real hierarchy (tree pane turns on automatically);
    // Dependencies cross phase boundaries; IsMilestone renders as a diamond.
    private List<GanttTask> _tasks = new() {
        new("discovery",  "Discovery & Planning", d.AddDays(-10), d.AddDays(-1), Progress: 100),
        new("interviews", "Stakeholder interviews", d.AddDays(-10), d.AddDays(-6), Progress: 100) { ParentId = "discovery" },
        new("requirements", "Requirements doc", d.AddDays(-7), d.AddDays(-3), Dependencies: new[] { "interviews" }) { ParentId = "discovery" },
        new("m-kickoff", "Kickoff approved", d.AddDays(-1), d.AddDays(-1), IsMilestone: true, Dependencies: new[] { "requirements" }) { ParentId = "discovery" },
        // ... Design / Build / Launch phases follow the same pattern
    };
}

examples.title: Drag to reschedule — with a real commit gate
examples.code:
<GanttChart @bind-Tasks="_tasks"
            ViewMode="GanttViewMode.Day"
            OnTaskUpdate="HandleTaskUpdate" />

@code {
    private IEnumerable<GanttTask> _tasks = new List<GanttTask> { /* ... */ };

    // OnTaskUpdate is a GATE, not a notification — it runs BEFORE the edit
    // commits and returns a GanttUpdateResult:
    //   false                                -> reject, nothing commits
    //   true                                 -> accept exactly as proposed
    //   GanttUpdateResult.AcceptWith(adjust)  -> accept, but snap Start/End/Progress
    private GanttUpdateResult HandleTaskUpdate(GanttTaskUpdate update)
    {
        if (update.Task.Start < DateTime.Today)
            return false; // reject — can't schedule into the past

        if (update.Task.Start.DayOfWeek != DayOfWeek.Monday)
        {
            var offset = ((int)update.Task.Start.DayOfWeek + 6) % 7;
            return GanttUpdateResult.AcceptWith(new GanttUpdateAdjustment(
                Start: update.Task.Start.AddDays(-offset),
                End: update.Task.End.AddDays(-offset)));
        }

        return true; // accept as proposed
    }
}

parameters.name: Rows
parameters.description: The currently visible rows — same list GanttTree/GanttTimeline render against, so a collapsed-away task never produces an arrow (see remarks above).

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: The active zoom level — feeds BarGeometry for each visible task.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: The timeline's date origin (first rendered column's date) — same value GanttTimeline computes as its own Origin.

parameters.name: ColumnWidth
parameters.description: The effective column width in pixels — same value GanttTimeline passes as its own EffectiveColumnWidth.

parameters.name: BarHeight
parameters.description: The effective bar height in pixels — same value GanttTimeline passes as its own EffectiveBarHeight.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: The overlay's pixel width — matches GanttTimeline's canvas TotalWidth.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: The overlay's pixel height — matches GanttTimeline's canvas CanvasHeight.

parameters.name: VisibleRowRange
parameters.description: The (inclusive) row-index range currently virtualized into view, with its own overscan margin already applied (Codex round 4, P2 #3) — arrows whose SOURCE and TARGET rows are BOTH outside this range are culled, matching the bars/tree pane this layer overlays (both already virtualize via <Virtualize>). Null (the default, and the value used before the first scroll-position report arrives) disables culling entirely — every arrow renders, unchanged from prior behavior. An arrow with ONE endpoint in range is deliberately kept (its visible endpoint still needs a line leading to/from it, matching how a bar half-scrolled off-screen still partially renders rather than vanishing outright).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the root <svg>.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Captures unmatched attributes and applies them to the root <svg>.

parameters.name: Task
parameters.description: The task/milestone this bar represents.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Left pixel offset within the timeline canvas, already resolved by the caller via DateToPixel. For a milestone this is the diamond's bounding-box left edge (center-column minus half the bar height), not the task's raw start-date pixel.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Pixel width of the bar (or, for a milestone, the diamond's square bounding box — equal to BarHeight).

parameters.name: RowIndex
parameters.description: Zero-based row slot within the timeline (mirrors v2's rowSlot — may differ from the task's index when group header rows are interleaved by a future task).

parameters.name: BarHeight
parameters.description: Bar height in pixels. Defaults to DefaultBarHeight.

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Per-task colour override (hex, rgb, or a CSS variable reference) — mirrors v2's BarColor delegate output. Null falls back to the theme's chart palette (--color-chart-1) — deliberately NOT --color-primary: the Gantt's default bar fill must follow chart theming (independent of the brand/accent colour), same as the rest of Lumeo's charts, rather than silently repainting every bar whenever a consumer changes their primary colour. ResolveGroupColorVar's own ColorByGroup per-group palette sits above this same token family.

parameters.name: BarTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the bar's default label content when set. Not used for milestones (v2 parity: milestones always show their name next to the diamond).

parameters.name: DragGhostTemplate
parameters.description: Overrides the drag ghost's rendered CONTENT (design spec Phase 3, T8). Null (the default) keeps the prior behavior — gantt-v3.js's makeGhost clones this bar's own rendered markup. When set, a HIDDEN sibling template carrying this fragment's output is cloned instead — see the markup's own remarks for the full coordinate-space contract (byte-identical position/size to the real bar; only the ghost's visual content differs). Applies to move/resize/progress drags of THIS bar, including for a milestone.

parameters.name: OnTaskClick
parameters.description: Raised when the bar is activated via mouse click OR keyboard (Enter/Space on the now-focusable bar — Codex round 4, P2 #5). Same contract as v2's Gantt.OnTaskClick (EventCallback<GanttTask>).

parameters.name: FocusedTaskId
parameters.description: Roving-tabindex target (arrow-key navigation — GanttV3's own accessibility gap, closed alongside wheel zoom). Every bar defaults to tabindex="0" when this is null (preserves EXACT prior behavior for a standalone GanttBar, e.g. every existing bUnit test that renders one in isolation with no GanttTimeline wrapping it). When set by GanttTimeline (which always sets it once ANY bar exists), only the bar whose Task's id matches gets tabindex="0" — every other bar gets -1, so a single Tab reaches exactly ONE bar instead of every bar in the chart, and arrow keys move which one that is.

parameters.name: OnKeyNavigation
parameters.description: Raised on ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (never Enter/Space — those stay OnTaskClick's own). Always wired by GanttTimeline (not a consumer-facing opt-in — arrow navigation works out of the box on every chart), so a bar rendered through it always has onkeydown attached even when OnTaskClick itself has no delegate. A standalone GanttBar with neither delegate set keeps its exact prior "no onkeydown at all" behavior.

parameters.name: Selected
parameters.description: Marks this bar as the selected occurrence (styling-hooks audit — ReUI parity's data-selected). Independent of Task itself: the caller decides what "selected" means (SelectedIds membership, when wired through GanttTimeline — see that component's own SelectedIds parameter). Default false, so a standalone GanttBar (no caller ever set this) renders byte-identically to before this parameter existed — no data-selected attribute at all, not merely one set to a falsy value (see WrapperAttributes's own remarks on the presence-vs-value convention every new styling-hook attribute here follows).

parameters.name: Now
parameters.description: The current date+time backing data-past (styling-hooks audit — ReUI parity). Null (the default) falls back to Now (the SERVER's local time) — the same standalone-usage fallback Now/Today already give when no GanttChart wraps the component. GanttTimeline forwards its own already browser-resolved EffectiveNow here (the SAME value NowIndicator's marker position uses — see that parameter's own remarks for why "browser time, not server time" matters: a server-rendered/prerendered chart has no business deciding what is "past" from a clock in a different time zone than the person looking at it), so this is never a second, independently resolved "now".

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the positioned wrapper.

parameters.name: Readonly
parameters.description: Disables the progress handle (design spec Phase 2, T2 — v2 parity: Gantt.Readonly/GanttTimeline.Readonly). Threaded down from GanttTimeline's own Readonly parameter — mirrors gantt-v2.js's own if (!readonly) { progressHandle = ... } (never creating the handle element at all when readonly, gantt-v2.js:555). Default false (interactive).

parameters.name: SuppressPointerClick
parameters.description: Suppresses this bar's OWN native onclick wiring while still keeping onkeydown (Enter/Space) active (design spec Phase-1/Phase-2 reconciliation fix — CRITICAL: OnTaskClick double-firing on every non-readonly pointer click). GanttTimeline registers its OWN JS-driven delegated pointerdown listener whenever it isn't Readonly (gantt-v3.js's ganttV3.registerDrag), which ALREADY discriminates a below-threshold click from a drag and invokes NotifyTaskClick exactly once per pointer click — independently of this component's own native onclick, which would otherwise ALSO fire for the identical physical click. GanttTimeline sets this to true for every bar it renders once its own engine's registration has actually been CONFIRMED (its interop register call returned without throwing — see GanttTimeline.SyncDragRegistrationAsync's own remarks), not merely whenever !Readonly (registration never depends on AllowCreate/CanDrop, only on Readonly). Bug fix (Codex P2 finding "Keep pointer clicks when drag interop is unavailable"): a custom IComponentInteropService that never overrides GanttV3RegisterDragAsync (inheriting its default no-op), or a register call that genuinely throws, previously left this permanently true with no delegated listener ever attached — pointer clicks were dead forever even though keyboard activation kept working. false when readonly (no engine is ever registered there, so this component's own native onclick remains the ONLY pointer-click path) OR while registration is still pending or has failed. Default false so a caller rendering GanttBar directly (standalone, no GanttTimeline — including every existing bUnit test that clicks a bar in isolation, with no real gantt-v3.js engine to fall back on) keeps its exact prior click-fires-once behavior unchanged. Keyboard activation (Enter/Space) NEVER routes through gantt-v3.js's pointer engine at all (it only ever listens for pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup), so onkeydown is never suppressed by this flag — there is no double-fire risk there to guard against.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Captures unmatched attributes and applies them to the positioned wrapper.

events.name: OnTaskClick
events.description: Raised when the bar is activated via mouse click OR keyboard (Enter/Space on the now-focusable bar — Codex round 4, P2 #5). Same contract as v2's Gantt.OnTaskClick (EventCallback<GanttTask>).

events.name: OnKeyNavigation
events.description: Raised on ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (never Enter/Space — those stay OnTaskClick's own). Always wired by GanttTimeline (not a consumer-facing opt-in — arrow navigation works out of the box on every chart), so a bar rendered through it always has onkeydown attached even when OnTaskClick itself has no delegate. A standalone GanttBar with neither delegate set keeps its exact prior "no onkeydown at all" behavior.

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: The active zoom level. Two-way bindable via ViewModeChanged.

parameters.name: ViewModeChanged
parameters.description: Raised when the user picks a new zoom level from the toolbar.

parameters.name: ZoomLevels
parameters.description: Restricts which zoom buttons render, in the given order. Null/empty shows the full default set (Day, Week, Month, Year) — mirrors v2's Gantt.razor ZoomLevels contract exactly, including the QuarterDay/HalfDay exclusion (no toolbar-representable label for either).

parameters.name: PeriodLabel
parameters.description: The current period's title (e.g. "January 2026"), computed by whatever owns the GanttState's VisibleRange.

parameters.name: TrailingContent
parameters.description: Extra content rendered after the zoom switcher (design spec Phase 3, T8 — v2 parity with Gantt.TrailingContent, the slot a GanttSettingsMenu companion plugs into). Null (the default) renders nothing extra.

parameters.name: OnToday
parameters.description: Raised when Today is clicked — the owner recenters VisibleRange on today.

parameters.name: OnPrevious
parameters.description: Raised when the previous-period button is clicked — the owner shifts VisibleRange back by the view mode's step.

parameters.name: OnNext
parameters.description: Raised when the next-period button is clicked — the owner shifts VisibleRange forward by the view mode's step.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the root toolbar element.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Captures unmatched attributes and applies them to the root toolbar element.

events.name: ViewModeChanged

events.description: Raised when Today is clicked — the owner recenters VisibleRange on today.

events.name: OnPrevious

events.name: OnNext

parameters.name: ShowRowCheckboxes
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors ShowRowCheckboxes. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: ShowSummaryBars
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors ShowSummaryBars. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: ShowZoomControl
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors ShowZoomControl. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: ShowOffscreenIndicators
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors ShowOffscreenIndicators, INCLUDING its default-true (this menu's own uncontrolled fallback matches GanttChart's real default deliberately, so a menu rendered before any user interaction reflects reality even when unbound).

parameters.name: InfiniteScroll
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors InfiniteScroll, INCLUDING its default-true (design spec Phase 3, T9 — same "this menu's uncontrolled fallback matches GanttChart's real default deliberately" precedent ShowOffscreenIndicators above already established), so a menu rendered before any user interaction reflects reality even when unbound.

parameters.name: NowIndicator
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors NowIndicator. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: MarkOffDays
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors MarkOffDays. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: Readonly
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors Readonly. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: AllowCreate
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors AllowCreate. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: AllowRowReorder
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors AllowRowReorder. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: FirstDayOfWeek
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors FirstDayOfWeek. Controlled-ness is decided by THIS parameter's own nullability (not FirstDayOfWeekChanged's HasDelegate — see the class remarks for why nullable settings use this idiom, unlike the plain-bool ones above). Null (the default, both as a parameter and as this menu's own internal fallback) is "culture-derived" — the toggle group still shows the resolved day pressed (see DisplayFirstDayOfWeek), it is simply not an EXPLICIT choice yet.

parameters.name: OffDays
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors OffDays. Same nullability-based controlled-ness as FirstDayOfWeek. Null is "culture-derived" (see DisplayOffDays for what actually renders pressed); an EXPLICIT empty set (every day toggled off) is a genuinely different, valid value — "zero off days" — and is never silently coerced back to null (see HandleOffDaysToggledAsync's own remarks).

parameters.name: ColorByGroup
parameters.description: Two-way bindable — mirrors ColorByGroup. Uncontrolled default false.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the popover panel's inner content wrapper.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Captures unmatched attributes and applies them to the popover panel.

parameters.name: Rollup
parameters.description: The computed (already-sanitized — see GanttRollupModel.SafeInvokeRollupMath) rollup this strip visualizes.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Left pixel offset within the timeline canvas, resolved by the caller from Rollup's Start/End the same way GanttScale.BarGeometry resolves a task's.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Pixel width of the strip.

parameters.name: RowIndex
parameters.description: Zero-based row slot within the timeline (same coordinate space as GanttBar.RowIndex).

parameters.name: BarHeight
parameters.description: Strip height in pixels. Defaults to SummaryBarHeight.

parameters.name: SummaryTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the strip's default (bg + fill + % label) content when set — the REUI "summary renderer" slot (design spec Phase 3, T3).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the positioned wrapper.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Captures unmatched attributes and applies them to the positioned wrapper.

parameters.name: Tasks
parameters.description: The tasks (and milestones) rendered as bars, in display order. Ignored when Rows is set.

parameters.name: Rows
parameters.description: The already-flattened, collapse-filtered row list (design spec Phase 2, T3's tree-pane/hierarchy row model — see GanttRowModel) — the same list a sibling GanttTree renders against, so both panes stay row-for-row aligned. When set, this takes priority over Tasks (which may still include header-hidden/collapsed tasks the caller never meant to show). When null (T2's original contract, still exercised by callers with no grouping/hierarchy), each entry of Tasks becomes its own row, 1:1, in list order — unchanged from T2's behavior.

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: The active zoom level — determines column width/unit/header format via GanttScale.

parameters.name: ViewModeChanged
parameters.description: Raised when GanttZoomControl's floating +/- stepper (design spec Phase 3, T7 — ShowZoomControl) picks a new zoom level. Same idea as GanttNav.ViewModeChanged — this component has no GanttState reference of its own (see the class remarks), so GanttChart wires BOTH GanttNav.ViewModeChanged and this to the SAME HandleViewModeChangedAsync method (the identical claim/reconcile/settle pipeline every view-mode change already routes through — GanttState.SetViewMode's own T4 remarks establish the precedent of one shared method, multiple callers) rather than inventing a second mutation path for a second UI surface.

parameters.name: RangeStart
parameters.description: The materialized date window's start (inclusive).

parameters.name: RangeEnd
parameters.description: The materialized date window's end (inclusive).

parameters.name: BarHeight
parameters.description: Override the pixel height of each task bar. Defaults to DefaultBarHeight.

parameters.name: ColumnWidth
parameters.description: Override the pixel width of each date column for the current view mode.

parameters.name: TodayHighlight
parameters.description: Highlight today with an accent header label, header dot, and full-column tint. Default true. Master switch (design spec Phase 3, T2) — the SAME parameter that gated the old line-only look now gates the whole upgraded treatment; nothing else needs a separate opt-in.

parameters.name: FirstDayOfWeek
parameters.description: Explicit first-day-of-week override for the Day ISO week-band upper header (design spec Phase 3, T2 — see UpperRuns's own firstDayOfWeek parameter). Null (the default) derives it from CurrentCulture. Ignored by every OTHER view mode.

parameters.name: OffDays
parameters.description: The week days treated as "off" for MarkOffDays's column tint (design spec Phase 3, T2). Null (the default) derives a region-appropriate set from CurrentCulture via DefaultOffDays — see its own remarks for the CLDR-sourced weekend table (NOT hardcoded Saturday/Sunday).

parameters.name: MarkOffDays
parameters.description: Tints OffDays columns (design spec Phase 3, T2 — "Mark off days"). Default false — no v2 equivalent, opt-in like every other REUI-parity addition with no v2 precedent. Only rendered for day-granularity view modes — see SupportsOffDayMarking.

parameters.name: NowIndicator
parameters.description: Renders a precise current-TIME line in sub-day view modes (design spec Phase 3, T2 — distinct from TodayHighlight's whole-DAY column treatment). Default false (opt-in). Only rendered for Hour-unit view modes (QuarterDay/HalfDay) — see SupportsNowIndicator.

parameters.name: Now
parameters.description: The browser-resolved current date+time backing NowIndicator (design spec Phase 3, T2 — same "caller resolves via JS, this component just renders the resolved value" pattern Today already uses). Null (the default) falls back to Now (the SERVER's local time) — the same standalone-usage fallback Today gives when no GanttChart wraps this component.

parameters.name: BarColor
parameters.description: Per-task bar colour override — see Lumeo.Gantt's v2 Gantt.BarColor for the contract.

parameters.name: BarTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces a bar's default label content when set.

parameters.name: OnTaskClick
parameters.description: Raised when a bar is activated via click or keyboard (Enter/Space) — forwarded from every rendered GanttBar (Codex round 4, P2 #5). Same contract as v2's Gantt.OnTaskClick.

parameters.name: SelectedIds
parameters.description: The selected LEAF task ids (styling-hooks audit — ReUI parity's data-selected). GanttChart forwards its own SelectedIds here — the SAME set GanttTree's row checkboxes already read/write (design spec Phase 3, T6) — so a bar's data-selected attribute can never disagree with the tree pane's own checkbox state for the identical task. Default empty (no GanttChart wrapping — or a standalone GanttTimeline that never wires this — renders every bar unselected, matching every existing render before this parameter existed: no caller ever set it, so GanttBar.Selected was never true anywhere in the tree, byte-identical to today).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the root scroll container.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Captures unmatched attributes and applies them to the root scroll container.

parameters.name: ScrollToTodayRequestId
parameters.description: The scroll-intent version (Codex round 14). GanttChart bumps it each time it issues a recenter (Today nav, a view-mode/geometry recenter, an emptiness transition). Purely a change-token — only "did it change since the last render" matters — so GanttTimeline knows to re-center the DOM's horizontal scroll (recentering VisibleRange alone doesn't move scrollLeft; see ScrollToCenterAsync). The paired ScrollTargetDate is honored ONCE per bump and then expires (see ResolveScrollTargetX). Left at its default (0) by any caller that never wires this — a standalone GanttTimeline never sees it fire again after the first-render center.

parameters.name: Today
parameters.description: "Today", resolved by the caller (Codex round 2, P2 #9 — see GanttChart's remarks). Defaults to Today (the SERVER's local date) so a caller using GanttTimeline standalone without GanttChart keeps its exact prior behavior; GanttChart instead passes down the BROWSER's local date once JS interop resolves it, for v2 parity (v2 derives "today" via the browser's own new Date()).

parameters.name: ScrollTargetDate
parameters.description: Overrides which date the scroll-to-center mechanism (ScrollToTodayRequestId, firstRender, empty→populated) actually scrolls toward. Null (the default) targets Today, unchanged from every existing behavior. Set by GanttChart specifically when recentering after a view-mode switch (Codex round 4, P2 #8) — the user's previously-centered date, not necessarily today. Today itself still drives the MARKER's own position (TodayInRange/TodayColumnStyle) — this only redirects where the DOM actually scrolls to.

parameters.name: ScrollTargetXOverride
parameters.description: Design spec Phase 3, T9 — a PIXEL-precise override for ResolveScrollTargetX, timeline-origin-relative (the SAME space that method's own GanttScale.DateToPixel return value already lives in). When set (and while the SAME intent this render's ScrollTargetDate pairs with is still pending), takes priority over deriving the target from ScrollTargetDate. Exists for exactly one caller today: GanttChart.HandleRangeExtensionRequestAsync's leading-edge recenter. Every OTHER scroll intent in this codebase (view-mode switches, Today, Previous/Next, an off-screen-chip click, GanttState.ScrollToDateAsync) is perfectly well served by a captured DATE re-projected through GanttScale.DateToPixel under the new geometry — accurate to within a fraction of a column, which is why those paths' own E2E coverage uses a several-pixel tolerance. A leading-edge extension is different: this task's own explicit ±1px proof requirement cannot be met that way, because DateToPixel's Day/Month/Year branches all read DateTime.Date — a date captured via PixelToDateContinuous (which DOES preserve a sub-unit fraction, e.g. a fractional day) LOSES that fraction the moment it is re-projected back through DateToPixel, up to nearly one whole column's worth of pixels (confirmed empirically via this task's own local E2E gate: an 11px drift on a 38px Day-mode column). Bypassing the DateTime round trip entirely — read the LIVE logical scroll center as a raw pixel value, add the ANALYTICALLY exact origin-shift delta (GanttScale.DateToPixel's own provable origin-linearity — see that method's remarks), done — has no such loss, because no DateTime intermediary is ever involved. Still exactly zero new interop surface and zero new GanttScale math: both the read (GanttV3GetScrollCenterXAsync) and the eventual write (GanttV3ScrollToXAsync, via this component's own existing ScrollToCenterAsync) are the SAME calls every other recenter already uses; this parameter only changes which VALUE gets handed to the write.

parameters.name: ScrollHostLeadingOffset
parameters.description: Pixels of the ScrollHost's own content that precede this timeline's origin (x=0) — namely a sibling tree pane's width, when GanttChart renders one (Codex round 4, P2 #2). Defaults to 0 (standalone mode, or no tree pane — this timeline's own coordinate space already starts at the ScrollHost's content origin). Added to every scroll TARGET before issuing it to centerOn — this timeline's own internal pixel math (bar/grid/marker positions) is entirely unaffected, since those are all relative to THIS component's own origin, not the shared pane's.

parameters.name: LeadingPaneWidth
parameters.description: Width (px) of a sibling tree pane, when GanttChart renders one — design spec Phase 3, T7. Real bug found via this campaign's own E2E gate: the "before" off-screen indicator chip's position:sticky pins to this timeline's own LOGICAL-start edge — the SAME logical edge GanttTree's own root pins to (sticky start-0) — so without an explicit offset the two land in the EXACT SAME on-screen spot (confirmed live: a "before" chip's own getBoundingClientRect() matched a tree-row grip's pixel-for- pixel), silently swallowing every pointer event meant for the tree pane underneath it — including, in the E2E suite, row-reorder drags. Deliberately a SEPARATE parameter from ScrollHostLeadingOffset, not a reuse of it: that one is PHYSICAL and LTR-only by design (0 under RTL, because the shared pane's own flex row already reverses there — see its own remarks). GanttTree.RootClass's start-0 is LOGICAL, so it pins to the SAME logical edge (physical-right under RTL) regardless of the flex reversal — meaning the tree pane's own footprint on the "before"/start-anchored chip is present in BOTH directions, which ScrollHostLeadingOffset alone cannot express (it collapses to 0 in exactly the case — RTL — where this value must NOT). Only ever added to the "before" chip's own inline-start offset; nothing pins to the opposite (end) edge, so an "after" chip needs no equivalent adjustment. Defaults to 0 (standalone mode, or no tree pane shown).

parameters.name: ScrollHost
parameters.description: The element that owns horizontal (and vertical) scrolling for this timeline, when a caller (namely GanttChart) provides one of its own. Null (the default) keeps this component's PRIOR, fully self-contained behavior: .lumeo-gantt-v3-canvas-scroll gets its own overflow-x-auto and every scroll interop call targets it directly — unchanged for any existing standalone usage (e.g. a bUnit test that renders GanttTimeline alone, with no GanttChart wrapping it).

parameters.name: Readonly
parameters.description: Disables drag-to-move/-resize (design spec Phase 2, T1 — v2-parity Readonly). Default false (interactive). Gates the CALL SITE: when true, SyncDragRegistrationAsync never calls Lumeo.Services.IComponentInteropService.GanttV3RegisterDragAsync{T} at all — no pointer listener is ever attached, matching the plan's "no listeners at all when readonly" requirement (not merely "listeners that no-op").

parameters.name: OnTaskUpdate
parameters.description: Raised once, on drop, after a drag-move/-resize commits (design spec Phase 2, T1's unified commit gate — GanttTaskUpdate(Task, Source)). GanttChart subscribes to this to update its GanttState and re-raise its OWN OnTaskUpdate/OnDateChange/ TasksChanged — this component never touches GanttState itself (same bubbling contract as OnToggleCollapse).

parameters.name: CanDrop
parameters.description: Live scheduling drag-drop validator (design spec Phase 2, T2 — the REUI canDropEvent analog, applied to move/resize dragging). When set, the JS drag engine calls ValidateDrop at most once per SNAPPED position change during a move/resize drag (never for a progress drag — see GanttScheduleDropContext's remarks) and paints the ghost as invalid when this predicate returns false; dropping on an invalid position reverts silently (no OnTaskUpdate, no commit). When null (the default), BuildDragOptions tells the JS side so via hasCanDrop: false — NO ValidateDrop calls happen at all, not even once.

parameters.name: AllowCreate
parameters.description: Opt-in drag-create on empty track background (design spec Phase 2, T3 — a REUI-parity addition; v2 has no drag-create at all, so the default is false, which keeps a v3 chart's interaction surface strict v2 parity until a caller explicitly opts in). When true (and not Readonly), a pointer-down on a row's empty track background (never a bar — see the row canvas markup's own per-task-row data-gantt-row-track div, in RowItems's Virtualize item template, for the hit-test ordering) followed by a horizontal drag paints a create-ghost spanning the snapped range, committing via CommitCreate on release. Readonly WINS over this unconditionally: when readonly, NO listeners are ever registered at all (see SyncDragRegistrationAsync), so a readonly chart never creates regardless of this flag's value — the same "no listeners at all, not merely listeners that no-op" contract T1 established for move/resize.

parameters.name: ShowSummaryBars
parameters.description: Renders a duration-weighted REUI-style envelope strip on every hierarchy-parent or flat-group row (design spec Phase 3, T3 — "Summary rollup bars, duration-weighted"). Default false: a deliberate v3-look delta from REUI (which defaults its own summaryBars prop to true) — see the Phase-3 ledger entry for the full reasoning. Turning this off entirely skips ComputeRollups (see Rollups), so an existing chart with hierarchy/GroupBy already in use pays nothing for the feature until it opts in.

parameters.name: RollupMath
parameters.description: Overrides the default duration-weighted rollup math (design spec Phase 3, T3 — "Overridable rollup math"; the REUI getSummaryProgress analog). Invoked once per eligible parent/group row with that row's DIRECT children — see GanttRollupModel's own remarks for exactly what "direct children" means for a nested hierarchy parent (transitivity via substitution, not a flattened descendant list) and for the defensive contract a throwing or out-of-range-returning override gets wrapped in regardless (GanttRollupModel.SafeInvokeRollupMath) — a broken override degrades to the default math for that one row, it never takes the rest of the chart down. null (the default) uses DefaultRollupMath for every row.

parameters.name: SummaryTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces a summary strip's default (bg + fill + % label) content when set (design spec Phase 3, T3 — the REUI renderSummary analog). null (the default) uses GanttSummaryBar's own built-in rendering.

parameters.name: ColorByGroup
parameters.description: Assigns each task a stable per-group var(--color-chart-1..5) bar colour when BarColor is null (design spec Phase 3, T7 — "default palette assigns stable per-group colors ... when BarColor is null"). Default false — see the Phase-3 ledger entry for the full "opt-in like every other REUI-parity addition with no v2 precedent" reasoning (ShowSummaryBars above already established the identical default posture for the same reason). The "group" is the task's own reorder bucket — see ResolveGroupColorVar for the exact key and its cross-reorder/cross-render stability proof.

parameters.name: ShowOffscreenIndicators
parameters.description: Renders a small directional chip at a row's edge when that row's bar is entirely outside the current horizontal scroll viewport, clicking it scrolls the bar back into view (design spec Phase 3, T7 — "Off-screen indicator chips ... direction arrow + click scrolls the bar into view"). Default true — DELIBERATELY the one exception to this campaign's "new look-changing REUI-parity features default off" precedent (ShowSummaryBars/NowIndicator/ MarkOffDays all opt-in): the plan text explicitly pins this one to REUI's own default-true, and unlike those three, an off-screen chip is a NAVIGATION AID whose absence is a silent discoverability regression (a bar scrolled out of view with no affordance to find it again), not a purely cosmetic surface a consumer's existing visual-snapshot baseline could be surprised by — the chip only ever appears in direct response to the VIEWER's own scroll action, never as part of a chart's initial/at-rest look, so there is no "chart looked different on upgrade with no code change" risk the opt-in precedent exists to prevent in the first place. See the Phase-3 ledger entry for the full reasoning.

parameters.name: ShowZoomControl
parameters.description: Renders a floating +/- zoom control in the canvas corner, stepping through ZoomLevels (design spec Phase 3, T7 — "Floating zoom control ... in addition to the toolbar switcher"). Default false — an ADDITIONAL, purely decorative UI surface (unlike ShowOffscreenIndicators's navigation-aid argument above, a toolbar zoom switcher already exists via GanttNav in every existing v3 chart) that changes a chart's at-rest visual footprint the moment it renders — the standard opt-in posture applies here exactly as it did for ShowSummaryBars.

parameters.name: ZoomLevels
parameters.description: Restricts which zoom levels GanttZoomControl steps through when ShowZoomControl is on — same contract (including the default full Day/Week/Month/Year set and the Quarter-must-be-explicitly-opted-in rule) as GanttNav.ZoomLevels, which this deliberately mirrors rather than reimplements (see GanttZoomControl's own remarks).

parameters.name: WheelZoom
parameters.description: Ctrl/Cmd + wheel over the timeline zooms, anchored on the pointer position (ReUI parity — wheelZoom, defaulting true). A BARE wheel is never touched (no listener decision even looks at it beyond the ctrl/meta check) — the page/pane keeps scrolling exactly as it would with no Gantt on it at all, which is the entire reason ReUI requires the modifier rather than hijacking plain wheel. At the current ZoomLevels list's own zoom limits (already at the finest/coarsest resolved level) the gesture is left alone entirely — no preventDefault — so the BROWSER's own ctrl/cmd+wheel page-zoom takes over instead of the gesture being silently swallowed. Steps through the SAME resolved GanttZoomLevelModel list GanttZoomControl/GanttNav already step through (see GanttZoomLevelModel's own "shared, never duplicated" remarks) — a discrete stepper, not a continuous zoom factor: GanttV3's zoom model is ALREADY a fixed 4-5 mode ladder (Day/Week/Month/[Quarter]/Year), unlike ReUI's own continuous 0.5-3 factor grafted onto a single view. Introducing a second, continuous "zoom factor" alongside that existing discrete model would be a much larger, orthogonal change (a new persisted scale dimension every other GanttV3 pixel computation would need to multiply through) for a gesture that, discretely stepped, already reads as "zoom" to a user — stepping is the right fit for THIS scale model, not a compromise.

parameters.name: OnWheelZoomRequested
parameters.type: EventCallback<(GanttViewMode Mode, DateTime AnchorDate, double AnchorOffsetPx)>
parameters.description: Raised instead of ViewModeChanged when a wheel-zoom gesture (WheelZoom) picks a new mode AND a richer host (GanttChart) is listening — carries the anchor date (under the OLD scale, at the pointer's content-space position) and the pointer's own local offset from the viewport's left edge, so the host can recenter the SAME date back under the pointer after the mode switch instead of merely preserving the viewport's CENTER (what every OTHER ViewMode trigger — the toolbar, an imperative SetViewMode — already does via GanttChart's own capture/recenter pipeline). Falls back to invoking ViewModeChanged directly (no anchor) when this has no delegate — a standalone GanttTimeline (no GanttChart wrapping it, so nothing to recenter with anyway) still gets basic wheel-zoom this way. Never invoked TOGETHER with ViewModeChanged for the SAME gesture (would race GanttChart's own mode-change guard, applying the intent twice and silently discarding whichever call lands second) — exactly one of the two fires.

parameters.name: ScrollTargetOffsetOverride
parameters.description: Pixel-precise offset (from the scroll viewport's own left edge) a pending ScrollTargetXOverride/ScrollTargetDate recenter should land at, INSTEAD of centerOn's usual viewport-CENTER placement — GanttChart's own wheel-zoom anchor preservation is the one caller (see OnWheelZoomRequested's remarks): every other recenter in this codebase genuinely wants the captured date centered, so this stays null for them, preserving their exact prior "center" behavior. Honored only while the SAME intent this render's ScrollTargetDate/ScrollToTodayRequestId pairs with is still pending — same one-shot-then-expires contract as ScrollTargetXOverride itself.

parameters.name: DragGhostTemplate
parameters.description: Overrides the drag ghost's rendered content for every bar (design spec Phase 3, T8). Passed straight through to DragGhostTemplate — see its own remarks for the full coordinate-space contract.

parameters.name: BarContextMenu
parameters.description: Renders a Lumeo ContextMenu at the pointer when a bar is right-clicked (design spec Phase 3, T8). Null (the default) leaves right-click on a bar alone — the browser's native context menu shows, exactly as before this parameter existed. Deliberately independent of Readonly — a context menu is a VIEW action, not an edit; see NotifyBarContextMenu's own remarks for the full reasoning and the drag-isolation contract (a right-click landing on a bar mid-gesture is swallowed entirely, never opens a menu).

parameters.name: InfiniteScroll
parameters.description: Nearing either horizontal edge of the currently-rendered range extends it by another page instead of dead-ending (design spec Phase 3, T9 — "horizontal infinite scroll ... replaces v2's fixed pad-before/after"). Default true (see the Phase-3 ledger entry, decision 1, for the full "what does an existing Phase-1 consumer actually notice" reasoning — the short version: nothing, until they scroll far enough to reach the ORIGINAL padded edge, at which point the timeline now keeps going instead of dead-ending). false restores exactly v2's own fixed pad-before/after — GanttChart's own ComputeInitialRange/ApplyPadding are COMPLETELY unchanged by this parameter; it only gates whether OnGanttV3VerticalScroll ever asks for MORE range once the user scrolls near what those already computed.

parameters.name: OnRangeExtensionRequested
parameters.description: Bubbles a "the user scrolled near an edge, please extend VisibleRange" request up to GanttChart (design spec Phase 3, T9) — this component never owns VisibleRange itself (it only ever RECEIVES RangeStart/RangeEnd as plain parameters, the same "GanttChart is the only place that touches GanttState" discipline every other bubbled edit in this file already follows — see OnTaskUpdate's own remarks), so it can only ask, never commit. true = the LEADING (earlier-dates) edge — the coordinate origin shifts, so the caller must recenter; false = TRAILING (later-dates) — a pure append, origin unchanged, no recenter needed. Not part of any consumer-facing contract (this component is only public because the Razor compiler forces it — see this file's own class remarks); wired internally by GanttChart only.

events.name: ViewModeChanged
events.description: Raised when GanttZoomControl's floating +/- stepper (design spec Phase 3, T7 — ShowZoomControl) picks a new zoom level. Same idea as GanttNav.ViewModeChanged — this component has no GanttState reference of its own (see the class remarks), so GanttChart wires BOTH GanttNav.ViewModeChanged and this to the SAME HandleViewModeChangedAsync method (the identical claim/reconcile/settle pipeline every view-mode change already routes through — GanttState.SetViewMode's own T4 remarks establish the precedent of one shared method, multiple callers) rather than inventing a second mutation path for a second UI surface.

events.name: OnTaskClick
events.description: Raised when a bar is activated via click or keyboard (Enter/Space) — forwarded from every rendered GanttBar (Codex round 4, P2 #5). Same contract as v2's Gantt.OnTaskClick.

events.name: OnTaskUpdate
events.description: Raised once, on drop, after a drag-move/-resize commits (design spec Phase 2, T1's unified commit gate — GanttTaskUpdate(Task, Source)). GanttChart subscribes to this to update its GanttState and re-raise its OWN OnTaskUpdate/OnDateChange/ TasksChanged — this component never touches GanttState itself (same bubbling contract as OnToggleCollapse).

events.name: OnWheelZoomRequested
events.type: EventCallback<(GanttViewMode Mode, DateTime AnchorDate, double AnchorOffsetPx)>
events.description: Raised instead of ViewModeChanged when a wheel-zoom gesture (WheelZoom) picks a new mode AND a richer host (GanttChart) is listening — carries the anchor date (under the OLD scale, at the pointer's content-space position) and the pointer's own local offset from the viewport's left edge, so the host can recenter the SAME date back under the pointer after the mode switch instead of merely preserving the viewport's CENTER (what every OTHER ViewMode trigger — the toolbar, an imperative SetViewMode — already does via GanttChart's own capture/recenter pipeline). Falls back to invoking ViewModeChanged directly (no anchor) when this has no delegate — a standalone GanttTimeline (no GanttChart wrapping it, so nothing to recenter with anyway) still gets basic wheel-zoom this way. Never invoked TOGETHER with ViewModeChanged for the SAME gesture (would race GanttChart's own mode-change guard, applying the intent twice and silently discarding whichever call lands second) — exactly one of the two fires.

Not part of any consumer-facing contract (this component is only public because the Razor compiler forces it — see this file's own class remarks); wired internally by GanttChart only.

parameters.name: Rows
parameters.description: The visible row list — identical to what's fed to GanttTimeline/GanttArrowLayer (design spec: single source of truth for row order/visibility).

parameters.name: OnToggleCollapse
parameters.description: Raised with a row's ToggleKey when its chevron is clicked. The owner (GanttChart) applies it via GanttState.ToggleCollapsed.

parameters.name: TreeColumns
parameters.description: Extra columns rendered after the pinned name column (design spec Phase 3, T5). Null/empty renders exactly the single name column.

parameters.name: TreeHeaderMenu
parameters.description: Slot rendered in the header row, after any column titles (design spec Phase 3, T5 — REUI "columns menu in header slot").

parameters.name: RowTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces a row's default label-cell content when set (design spec Phase 3, T5). The indent spacer and expander/toggle button are ALWAYS rendered by this component regardless — see the class remarks. Never invoked for a row with no Task.

parameters.name: ShowTaskMeta
parameters.description: Renders a second "date-range · N%" line under a row's name (2026-08-10 shadcn alignment plan, G6 — the reference always shows this; Lumeo showed the label only). Default false, matching this codebase's own convention for every optional display toggle added since Phase 3 (ShowSummaryBars/MarkOffDays/NowIndicator/ ColorByGroup all default off). Ignored when RowTemplate is set (the custom template already owns the entire name-cell content) or for a row with no Task (a flat-grouping GroupHeader row has no Start/End/Progress to show).

parameters.name: TreePaneWidth
parameters.description: The pinned name column's CURRENT resolved width in pixels. GanttChart owns clamping and the controlled-vs-uncontrolled resolution (see its own EffectiveTreePaneWidth) — this component only renders whatever it is handed and reports completed drag/keyboard gestures via OnResize.

parameters.name: OnResize
parameters.description: Raised once per completed splitter gesture (a pointer-drag release via CommitSplitterWidth, or a keyboard nudge) with the new width. NOT raised continuously while dragging — the live visual is JS-only (see SyncSplitterRegistrationAsync's own remarks).

parameters.name: Tasks
parameters.description: The full task list Rows was built from (design spec Phase 3, T6) — used to compute per-row checkbox tri-state (GanttSelectionModel) and reorder bucket/index (GanttReorderModel), BOTH of which must see descendants/siblings hidden behind a collapsed ancestor, unlike the already collapse-filtered Rows — mirrors GanttTimeline's own separate Tasks parameter for the identical reason (its own Rollups).

parameters.name: SelectedIds
parameters.description: Ids of currently-selected LEAF rows (design spec Phase 3, T6 — see GanttSelectionModel's own remarks for exactly which rows can be members). GanttChart owns SelectedIds' controlled/uncontrolled resolution and always hands this component the resolved, non-null set (never null here, even when nothing is selected — mirrors TreePaneWidth's own resolved-not-raw contract).

parameters.name: ShowRowCheckboxes
parameters.description: Renders a checkbox column when true (design spec Phase 3, T6 — REUI "Leaf row selection (checkboxes)"). Default false.

parameters.name: OnRowSelectionChange
parameters.description: Raised when a row's checkbox is toggled. Key is the leaf task's own id for a leaf row, or the row's ToggleKey (a hierarchy-parent task id, or a GroupToggleKey-prefixed group key) for a tri-state parent/group row; Selected is the checkbox's NEW value (true = select all, false = deselect all, for a parent/group row). GanttChart resolves Key into the actual leaf id(s) to flip via ResolveLeafIds.

parameters.name: AllowRowReorder
parameters.description: Enables drag-to-reorder tree rows (design spec Phase 3, T6 — REUI "Row reorder (drag tree rows)"). Default false. Reorder is confined to the dragged row's own "bucket" (same ParentId, or same GroupLabel in flat mode — see GanttReorderModel's own remarks); a cross-bucket move is never offered by the drag UI at all. Readonly blocks it unconditionally.

parameters.name: CanDropRow
parameters.description: Live validation predicate for a candidate row-reorder drop position (design spec Phase 3, T6 — the REUI canDropEvent analog applied to row reorder). Evaluated continuously while a reorder drag is in flight (ValidateRowDrop) and once more at drop (CommitRowReorder trusts the last live verdict — same two-phase discipline CanDrop/ ValidateDrop/CommitDrag already established). Null (default) permits every within-bucket position.

parameters.name: OnRowReorder
parameters.description: Raised once, after a completed row-reorder drop, with the resolved GanttRowReorder payload. GanttChart applies the equivalent list reorder (Move) AND re-raises the same payload through its own public OnRowReorder.

parameters.name: Readonly
parameters.description: Disables checkbox interaction and row-reorder dragging (design spec Phase 3, T6 — "Readonly blocks both"). Mirrors Readonly's own contract exactly: checked FRESH on every JSInvokable call (ValidateRowDrop/CommitRowReorder), not just at registration time — the Phase-2 lesson (a gesture already in flight at the moment of a runtime flip has its own move/up handlers living in gantt-v3.js's per-drag closure, which survives unregisterRowReorderDrag unaffected and still calls these on release/hover).
